claim: The tissue-like system recapitulates the dynamics of engineered primary human immune cells.
source: Here we report a tissue-like system that recapitulates the dynamics of engineered primary human immune cell.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental demonstrations throughout the manuscript including imaging and functional assays.

claim: The approach facilitates real-time single-cell manipulations, tracking of interactions and functional responses complemented by population-based measurements of cytokines, activation status and proliferation.
source: Our approach facilitates real-time single-cell manipulations, tracking of interactions and functional responses complemented by population-based measurements of cytokines, activation status and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated through various experiments shown in Figures 4 and 5, including imaging, flow cytometry, and ELISA measurements.

claim: The system recapitulates CD4 T-cells' help to CD8 T-cells through enhanced maturation of DCs.
source: As a proof of concept, we recapitulate immunological phenomenon such as CD4 T-cells' help to CD8 T-cells through enhanced maturation of DCs and the effect of PD-1 checkpoint blockades.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5B showing upregulation of CD86 on DCs and enhanced CD8 activation in the presence of CD4 T-cells.

claim: The system recapitulates the effect of PD-1 checkpoint blockades.
source: As a proof of concept, we recapitulate immunological phenomenon such as CD4 T-cells' help to CD8 T-cells through enhanced maturation of DCs and the effect of PD-1 checkpoint blockades.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5C-D showing enhanced clustering and activation with anti-PD-1 antibodies.

claim: The system characterizes unique dynamics of T-cell/DC interactions as a function of antigen affinity.
source: In addition, we characterise unique dynamics of T-cell/DC interactions as a function of antigen affinity.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4D showing different motility speeds with high vs low affinity peptides.

claim: Mouse models can only provide limited insight for advancing translational research despite their tremendous utility.
source: The field of human immunology has gained much attention in the last few decades with the increasing realisation that despite the tremendous utility of mouse models, they can only provide limited insight for advancing translational research (Wagar et al., 2018; Council MRC, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cell lines have diverged tremendously from primary cells, making their signalling machinery and response thresholds no longer representative.
source: Cell lines have diverged tremendously from primary cells, making their signalling machinery and response thresholds no longer representative (Colin-York et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Humanised mouse models have only a portion of their system 'humanised', rendering the remaining parts confounding factors.
source: humanised mouse models have only a portion of their system 'humanised', rendering the remaining parts confounding factors (Theocharides and Manz, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The toolkit achieves high efficiency TCR expression and maintenance of T-cell motility, activation dynamics and viability using mRNA electroporation.
source: We report a toolkit that achieves two critical goals for engineering T-cells: (1) high efficiency TCR expression and maintenance of T-cell motility, activation dynamics and viability using mRNA electroporation
evidence: This is demonstrated through multiple figures showing TCR expression efficiency (Figure 2), motility data (Figure 4), and viability measurements (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).

claim: The common approach to render T-cells antigen-specific relies on lentiviral transduction of the TCR, which requires prior expansion of T-cells.
source: The common approach to render T-cells antigen-specific relies on lentiviral transduction of the TCR, which requires prior expansion of T-cells to achieve high expression efficiency and hinders the study of natural quiescent populations, namely naïve and memory T-cells (Dai et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Reported approaches using electroporation suffer from low efficiency of expression, low viability, and impaired cell motility.
source: However, reported approaches using electroporation suffer from low efficiency of expression, low viability, and most importantly impaired cell motility, a critical consideration in the context of delivery to target tissues.
evidence: This is a statement about previous approaches that motivates the current work, and is implicitly supported by the comparison data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Using a square-wave electroporation apparatus, the 1G4 TCR can be expressed in naïve CD8 T-cells.
source: Using a square-wave electroporation apparatus, we are able to express the 1G4 TCR, specific to the NY-ESO tumour associated antigen (Chen et al., 2000) in naïve (Figure 2A) and memory (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) CD8 T-cells
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2A showing flow cytometry data of TCR expression.

claim: The 1G4 TCR is specific to the NY-ESO tumour associated antigen.
source: Using a square-wave electroporation apparatus, we are able to express the 1G4 TCR, specific to the NY-ESO tumour associated antigen (Chen et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The 1G4 TCR can be expressed in memory CD8 T-cells.
source: Using a square-wave electroporation apparatus, we are able to express the 1G4 TCR, specific to the NY-ESO tumour associated antigen (Chen et al., 2000) in naïve (Figure 2A) and memory (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) CD8 T-cells
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The 868 TCR specific for the HIV gag protein can be expressed in CD8 T-cells.
source: as well as the 868 TCR specific for the HIV gag protein (Varela-Rohena et al., 2008) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), both presented by HLA-A*0201.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and supported by citation.

claim: Successful pairing of the alpha and beta heterodimer of the TCR is important for the expression and assembly at the cell surface.
source: Successful pairing of the alpha and beta heterodimer of the TCR is important for the expression and assembly at the cell surface
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Cysteine modifications in the TCR chains achieve successful pairing of the alpha and beta heterodimer.
source: this was achieved by introducing cysteine modifications in the TCR chains (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and Table 1) (Cohen et al., 2007)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and supported by citation.

claim: Co-transfection with human CD3ζ improves TCR expression.
source: as well as co-transfection with the human CD3ζ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), as the endogenous protein is most likely sequestered by the endogenous TCR limiting the expression of the introduced TCR.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C showing increased expression with CD3ζ co-transfection.

claim: Naïve CD8 T-cells form a mature immunological synapse following TCR electroporation.
source: The functionality of naïve CD8 T-cells following TCR electroporation was confirmed by the formation of a mature immunological synapse in naïve and activated CD8 T-cells (IS, Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2B showing synapse formation on supported lipid bilayers.

claim: Activated CD8 T-cells form a mature immunological synapse following TCR electroporation.
source: The functionality of naïve CD8 T-cells following TCR electroporation was confirmed by the formation of a mature immunological synapse in naïve and activated CD8 T-cells (IS, Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: TCR-electroporated naïve CD8 T-cells upregulate the activation marker CD69.
source: and the upregulation of the activation marker CD69 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A showing dose response curves.

claim: The efficiency of TCR expression varied among donors with an average value of 81 ± 7% (mean ± SD, n = 13).
source: The efficiency of TCR expression varied among donors with an average value of 81 ± 7% (mean ± SD, n = 13)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from multiple donors.

claim: TCR electroporation achieves more than 90% cell viability.
source: with more than 90% cell viability and 80–90% cell recovery, both of which were severely reduced using alternative electroporation approaches (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: TCR electroporation achieves 80-90% cell recovery.
source: with more than 90% cell viability and 80–90% cell recovery, both of which were severely reduced using alternative electroporation approaches (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Alternative electroporation approaches severely reduce cell viability and recovery.
source: with more than 90% cell viability and 80–90% cell recovery, both of which were severely reduced using alternative electroporation approaches (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 comparing different electroporation methods.

claim: The induction of expression of an exogenous TCR in CD4 T-cells is considerably harder than in CD8 T-cells.
source: The induction of expression of an exogenous TCR in CD4 T-cells is considerably harder than in CD8 T-cells (Dai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Using natural sequences or cysteine modifications failed to induce expression of TCRs in naïve CD4 T-cells.
source: Using natural sequences or the introduction of cysteine modifications used for 1G4 and 868 failed to induce expression of TCRs in naïve CD4 T-cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental work.

claim: Replacing the constant region of the human TCR with that of mouse TCR allowed for successful chain pairing in naïve CD4 T-cells.
source: However, replacing the constant region of the human TCR with that of mouse TCR (Table 2) (Cohen et al., 2006) allowed for successful chain pairing and we were able to achieve expression in 72 ± 8.9% (mean ± SD, n = 15) of the cells
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally and supported by citation.

claim: TCR expression in naïve CD4 T-cells was achieved in 72 ± 8.9% (mean ± SD, n = 15) of cells using mouse constant regions.
source: we were able to achieve expression in 72 ± 8.9% (mean ± SD, n = 15) of the cells detected using H57 mAb against the mouse constant region of the β chain.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from multiple donors.

claim: Three different HLA-DPB1*04 restricted TCRs were successfully expressed in naïve CD4s: 6F9, R12C9, and SG6.
source: We have successful expressed three different HLA-DPB1*04 restricted TCRs in naïve CD4s: 6F9 (Figure 2C) and R12C9, both specific to the MAGE-A3 protein (Yao et al., 2016) and SG6 specific for NY-ESO (Zhao et al., 2006a) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, with citations for the TCR specificities.

claim: 6F9 and R12C9 TCRs are both specific to the MAGE-A3 protein.
source: 6F9 (Figure 2C) and R12C9, both specific to the MAGE-A3 protein (Yao et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: SG6 TCR is specific for NY-ESO.
source: and SG6 specific for NY-ESO (Zhao et al., 2006a)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The expression of SG6 was consistently lower than 6F9 and R12C9 in naïve CD4 T-cells.
source: The expression of SG6 was consistently lower than 6F9 and R12C9 in naïve CD4 T-cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A.

claim: When TCRs were electroporated into recently activated CD4 T-cells, high expression levels were achieved in 97.8 ± 1% (mean ± SD, n = 15) of the cells.
source: However, when the same TCRs were electroporated into recently activated CD4 T-cells, high expression levels were achieved in 97.8 ± 1% (mean ± SD, n = 15) of the cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from multiple donors shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The functionality of naïve CD4 T-cells upon TCR electroporation was confirmed by IS formation.
source: The functionality of the naïve CD4 T-cells upon TCR electroporation was confirmed by IS formation (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4C–D)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4C-D.

claim: The functionality of naïve CD4 T-cells upon TCR electroporation was confirmed by T-cell activation.
source: The functionality of the naïve CD4 T-cells upon TCR electroporation was confirmed by IS formation (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4C–D) and T-cell activation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Enhanced expression of the TCR in activated CD4 T-cells resulted in enhanced pMHC accumulation at the IS.
source: The enhanced expression of the TCR in activated CD4 T-cells resulted in enhanced pMHC accumulation at the IS (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 4D.

claim: Square-wave electroporation maintains the motile behaviour and interaction dynamics of naïve CD8 T-cells expressing 1G4 at similar levels to those of untouched cells.
source: Using the square-wave electroporator we were able to maintain the motile behaviour and interaction dynamics of naïve CD8 T-cells expressing 1G4, at similar levels to those of untouched cells, on 2D stimulatory 'spots' (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Video 1 and Mayya et al., 2018).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 5 and Video 1, with comparison to previous work.

claim: The closest model for bona fide DCs is monocyte-derived DCs (moDCs) with well-established protocols for their generation.
source: The closest model for bona fide DCs is monocyte-derived DCs (moDCs) with well-established protocols for their generation.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Classical moDC protocols have an extended duration (7–10 days).
source: The caveat with those protocols is their extended duration (7–10 days) (Zhou and Tedder, 1995)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Extended moDC generation time-frame may alter autologous T-cells' phenotype.
source: a time-frame which may alter autologous T-cells' phenotype.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the potential effects of extended culture.

claim: A 48 hr protocol was optimised to generate fully matured moDCs.
source: We therefore optimised a 48 hr protocol (Obermaier et al., 2003) to generate fully matured moDCs.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3 and supported by citation to the original protocol.

claim: The 'express' moDCs are able to upregulate MHC and other costimulatory molecules.
source: The 'express' moDCs are able to upregulate MHC and other costimulatory molecules and produce a similar profile of soluble factors as the 'classical' moDC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: The 'express' moDCs produce a similar profile of soluble factors as the 'classical' moDC.
source: The 'express' moDCs are able to upregulate MHC and other costimulatory molecules and produce a similar profile of soluble factors as the 'classical' moDC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Peptide loading on express moDCs achieved levels similar to those previously reported with other APCs.
source: We have also quantified peptide loading on these cells and achieved levels similar to those previously reported with other APCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) (Zehn et al., 2006).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and compared to previous literature.

claim: T-cells–DC interactions have been extensively studied in mice using explants and intravital imaging.
source: T-cells–DC interactions have been extensively studied in mice using explants and intravital imaging (Miller et al., 2002)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: T-cell-DC interaction studies using explants and intravital imaging are practically impossible in humans.
source: however, such studies are practically impossible in humans.
evidence: This is a statement about practical limitations in human research.

claim: Collagen I-based 3D matrices support the culture of human immune cells.
source: To achieve these goals we chose collagen I -based 3D matrices (Gunzer et al., 2000), which we optimised to support the culture of human immune cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout Figure 4 and supported by citation to previous work with collagen matrices.

claim: Culturing cells in the presence of human serum results in better basal motility than FBS.
source: Culturing cells in the presence of human serum results in better basal motility than FBS (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and Video 2, Table 3)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A comparing different serum conditions.

claim: Basal motility is significantly enhanced by the addition of homeostatic chemokines such as CCL19.
source: which is significantly enhanced by the addition of homeostatic chemokines such as CCL19 (Video 3), CCL21 and CXCL12 (Video 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4A and associated videos.

claim: Only CXCL12 was able to maintain high motility in cultures with FBS.
source: However, only CXCL12 was able to maintain high motility in cultures with FBS.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All collagens were equally good in supporting motility and interactions.
source: All collagens were equally good in supporting motility and interactions, while more advanced ECM may have a marginal advantage for motility.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B comparing different collagen sources.

claim: More advanced ECM may have a marginal advantage for motility.
source: All collagens were equally good in supporting motility and interactions, while more advanced ECM may have a marginal advantage for motility.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The use of bovine collagen-I as the 3D scaffold, with human serum, and CXCL12 provides an optimal 3D system with similar movement parameters to T-cells in mouse lymph nodes or explanted human tissues.
source: In our view, the use of bovine collagen-I as the 3D scaffold, with human serum, and CXCL12 to enhance motility provides an optimal 3D system with similar movement parameters to T-cells in mouse lymph nodes or explanted human tissues (Bougherara et al., 2015; Murooka et al., 2012; Salmon et al., 2012; Woolf et al., 2007).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data supported by comparison to previous literature.

claim: Lonza-Amaxa and ThermoFisher-Neon electroporation methods resulted in lower performance in cell recovery and protein expression.
source: We have also re-evaluated two additional electroporation methods, namely Lonza-Amaxa and ThermoFisher-Neon. In addition to their lower performance in cell recovery and protein expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Lonza-Amaxa and ThermoFisher-Neon electroporation methods resulted in poor motility dynamics within the 3D environment.
source: they further resulted in poor motility dynamics and hence activation of cells within the 3D environment, where the search for antigen loaded APCs becomes a confounding factor (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-F.

claim: T-cells move faster than acDCs in collagen gels.
source: Note the faster motility of T-cells compared to acDCs and similar motility using homeostatic chemokines (CCL19, CCL21 and CXCL12).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4A and Table 3.

claim: T-cells have similar motility using homeostatic chemokines CCL19, CCL21 and CXCL12.
source: Note the faster motility of T-cells compared to acDCs and similar motility using homeostatic chemokines (CCL19, CCL21 and CXCL12).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4A and Table 3.

claim: 1G4-expressing naïve CD8 T-cells upregulate CD69 following interaction with antigen-loaded acDCs in 3D collagen.
source: Snapshots from a time-lapse movie (Video 3) following the interactions of 1G4-expressing naïve CD8 T-cells (magenta) with antigen-loaded acDCs (green) in a collagen gel containing CXCL12, and the upregulation of CD69 is visible at T = 140 min following the accumulation of an anti-CD69 antibody on the surface of the cells (cyan, also in cyan are irrelevant CD4 T-cells).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4B and Video 3.

claim: 1G4-expressing CD8 T-cells flux calcium upon binding to antigen-loaded acDCs in 3D collagen.
source: Snapshots from a time-lapse movie (Video 4) showing three different 1G4-expressing CD8 T-cells (magenta), loaded with calcium dye Fluo4-AM (green), interacting with an antigen loaded acDC (100 nM NY-ESO-9V, cyan) in 3D collagen and fluxing calcium (green) upon binding.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4C and Video 4.

claim: Lower calcium flux is observed in second and third contacts suggesting lower antigen availability being sequestered by the primary synapse.
source: Note the lower flux in the second and third contacts suggesting lower antigen availability, being sequestered by the primary synapse.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: High affinity peptide NY-ESO-9V induces T-cell arrest.
source: A high affinity peptide, NY-ESO-9V, (Video 7) induced T-cell arrest
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4D showing reduced speed with 9V peptide.

claim: Lower affinity peptide NY-ESO-9L does not lead to stable contacts.
source: whereas a lower affinity peptide, NY-ESO-9L, (Video 8), led to similar dynamics non-peptide loaded (Video 9) where no stable contacts are formed.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4D and Videos 8-9.

claim: T-cells decelerate to 3 μm/min upon engaging with high affinity peptide compared to 12 μm/min for both null and 9L.
source: Note the deceleration of the cells upon engaging with high affinity peptide (3 μm/min compared to 12 μm/min for both null and 9L).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There are marginal differences in T-cell activation response relative to major differences in dynamics between high and low affinity peptides.
source: Since our 3D culture offers a relatively simple way to extract cells for flow cytometry and downstream analyses, we were able to correlate the interaction dynamics with the activation state of the cells and observe marginal differences in the response relative to the major differences in dynamics (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4E showing similar activation despite different dynamics.

claim: Good activation is achieved despite the absence of T-cell arrest with low affinity peptide NY-ESO-9L.
source: Note the good activation despite the absence of T-cell arrest with low affinity peptide (NY-ESO-9L).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4E.

claim: The 3D culture system enables monitoring of cytokine production.
source: Using our system, we were also able to monitor cytokine production (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The 3D culture system enables monitoring of proliferation.
source: proliferation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The 3D culture system enables monitoring of intracellular markers.
source: and intracellular markers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: DCs can be pre-loaded prior to or following gel polymerisation to mimic the delivery of antigen to lymph nodes.
source: In order to study the interaction dynamics of T-cells at different time points we could pre-load the DCs prior to or following gel polymerisation to mimic the delivery of antigen to lymph nodes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and Videos 10–11, respectively).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and Videos 10-11.

claim: The system can interrogate the dynamics of CD4 T-cells help to CD8 T-cells.
source: Our ability to engineer both CD4 and CD8 T-cells independently with different TCRs enables us to interrogate complex dynamics of a trinary cellular system whereby both types of T-cells can interact with similar or different APCs. We show here that using our system we can interrogate the dynamics of CD4 T-cells help to CD8 T-cells (Castellino et al., 2006) (Figure 5A, Video 12)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5A-B and Video 12, with citation to previous work on CD4 help.

claim: The activation of CD4 T-cells coincides with enhanced maturation of the DCs by upregulation of CD86.
source: where the activation of CD4 T-cells (Figure 5B, top) coincides with enhanced maturation of the DCs by upregulation of CD86 (Figure 5B, middle)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5B.

claim: The activation of CD4 T-cells coincides with enhanced activation of the CD8 T-cells.
source: where the activation of CD4 T-cells (Figure 5B, top) coincides with enhanced maturation of the DCs by upregulation of CD86 (Figure 5B, middle) and enhanced activation of the CD8 T-cells (Figure 5B, bottom).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5B.

claim: Memory CD8 T-cells form clusters around acDC in the presence of anti PD-1 blocking antibody Nivolumab compared to less tight contacts in the isotype control.
source: 1G4-expressing memory CD8 T-cells (magenta) co-cultured with acDCs loaded with 100 nM NY-ESO-9V (green). Cells form clusters around acDC in the presence of anti PD-1 blocking antibody Nivolumab (left) compared to less tight contacts in the isotype control (right).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5C.

claim: There is no change in the motility dynamics of memory CD8 T-cells with PD-1 checkpoint blockade.
source: Despite the lack of any change in the motility dynamics of the cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The presence of the checkpoint blockade enhances the clustering of CD8 T-cells around their targets.
source: there was a clear evidence that the presence of the checkpoint blockade enhances the clustering of CD8 T-cells around their targets (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5C.

claim: Enhanced activation with checkpoint blockade is only observable for late readouts such as 41BB expression and target cell killing.
source: This has also been corroborated by enhanced activation, although only observable for late readouts such as 41BB expression and target cell killing (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5D.

claim: Enhanced expression of PDL-1 on CD8 T-cells was observed following stimulation.
source: Interestingly, we saw an enhanced expression of PDL-1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), the ligand for PD-1, on CD8 T-cells
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Enhanced PDL-1 expression could lead to cis interactions that act as a cell intrinsic regulation mechanism.
source: which could lead to cis interactions that act as a cell intrinsic regulation mechanism (Sugiura et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the data and supported by citation.

claim: Differences exist between the pathways enhanced by the two blocking antibody clones EH12 and Nivolumab.
source: Surprisingly, we noted differences between the pathways enhanced by the two blocking antibody clones: EH12 seemed superior at enhancing surface markers, whereas Nivolumab outperformed EH12 in the killing assays.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5D comparing the two antibodies.

claim: EH12 seemed superior at enhancing surface markers.
source: EH12 seemed superior at enhancing surface markers, whereas Nivolumab outperformed EH12 in the killing assays.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5D.

claim: Nivolumab outperformed EH12 in the killing assays.
source: EH12 seemed superior at enhancing surface markers, whereas Nivolumab outperformed EH12 in the killing assays.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 5D.

claim: The experimental approach can be extended towards reconstitution of more complex biology such as tumour infiltrating lymphocytes and the role of regulatory T-cells in cancer.
source: Our experimental approach can be further extended towards reconstitution of more complex biology such as tumour infiltrating lymphocytes and the role of regulatory T-cells in cancer.
evidence: This is a speculation about future applications of the system.

claim: The mechanical and biophysical features introduced by the platform provide greater fidelity to in-vivo conditions.
source: We believe that the mechanical and biophysical features introduced by our platform provide greater fidelity to in-vivo conditions and will improve predictive power of pre-clinical studies in all human cell-based systems.
evidence: This is an interpretation and speculation about the advantages of the system.

claim: The platform will improve predictive power of pre-clinical studies in all human cell-based systems.
source: We believe that the mechanical and biophysical features introduced by our platform provide greater fidelity to in-vivo conditions and will improve predictive power of pre-clinical studies in all human cell-based systems.
evidence: This is a speculation about the impact of the system.

claim: The system should be integrated with other classical and computational approaches to enhance translational research.
source: We propose that our system should be integrated with other classical and computational approaches to enhance translational research.
evidence: This is a proposal for future use of the system.

claim: Cells were electroporated at 300 V, 2 ms in an ECM 830 Square Wave Electroporation System.
source: Cells were electroporated at 300 V, 2 ms in an ECM 830 Square Wave Electroporation System (BTX).
evidence: This is a methodological detail.

claim: For 10^6 CD8 T-cells, 2 μg of each TCRα, TCRβ and CD3ζ RNA was used.
source: For 106 cells CD8 T-cells, 2 μg of each TCRα, TCRβ and CD3ζ RNA was used.
evidence: This is a methodological detail.

claim: For 10^6 CD4 T-cells, 4 μg of TCRα and TCRβ was used.
source: For 106 CD4 T-cells, 4 μg of TCRα and TCRβ was used.
evidence: This is a methodological detail.

claim: Extended culture (>5 days) prior to electroporation results in marginal reduction in TCR expression efficiency.
source: Note, extended culture (>5 days) prior to electroporation also results in marginal reduction in TCR expression efficiency, although no reduction is observed for control GFP.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental work.

claim: The exogenous TCR can be detected up to 96 hr post electroporation.
source: The exogenous TCR can be detected up to 96 hr post electroporation.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental work.

claim: During the first 24 hr monocyte differentiation into DC was induced, followed by 24 hr maturation to get activated DCs.
source: During the first 24 hr monocyte differentiation into DC was induced, followed by 24 hr maturation to get activated DCs (acDCs) (Figure 3).
evidence: This describes the protocol shown in Figure 3.

claim: Extended culture in the 3D system leads to ~50% reduction in cell speed due to chemokine desensitisation.
source: Extended culture in the 3D system leads to ~50% reduction in cell speed due to chemokine desensitisation and can be overcome by the addition of fresh chemokine after 18 hr.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental work.

claim: The reduction in cell speed due to chemokine desensitisation can be overcome by the addition of fresh chemokine after 18 hr.
source: Extended culture in the 3D system leads to ~50% reduction in cell speed due to chemokine desensitisation and can be overcome by the addition of fresh chemokine after 18 hr.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental work.
